answer: Sybil resistance comes from a vouch graph: an agent counts only when already-trusted peers, each tied to a distinct payment origin, vouch for it. Clones can vouch only for one another, forming a dense cluster with no edge to the honest core, which graph analysis prunes. To slip in, an attacker must bribe genuinely separate agents to sponsor each puppet, paying a real fee per identity. A vine needs a rooted trunk to climb; a mirror can show many faces but not many distinct sponsors; a cedar ring of clones stays isolated, so each fake costs a bribe.
